_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Nicaragua covering Chorotegas/Nicarao indigenous peoples, Columbus/Spanish conquest, Granada/León rivalry, Walker filibuster+burning Granada 1856, independence 1821, liberal vs conservative wars, Zelaya liberal reforms, US interventions (1912-33, banana/canal interests), Augusto Sándino resistance (original Sandinista), Somoza Dynasty 1936-79 (43 years), Sandinista Revolution 1979, FSLN (Ortega), Contra War (Reagan's 'freedom fighters', Iran-Contra), Chamorro presidency, and Ortega dictatorship (2007-present).

country_profile.government_type: Unitary presidential constitutional republic (de jure authoritarian regime de facto)

religion.note: Rapid evangelicalization; Sandinista-Catholic tensions (1980s liberation theology vs hierarchy); Moravian Church (Caribbean coast, indigenous peoples); Ortega wife Rosario Murillo co-president with cult-like mysticism

ethnic_groups.name: Mestizo
ethnic_groups.notes: Mixed Indigenous-European; dominant Pacific/central region; Spanish-speaking

ethnic_groups.name: White
ethnic_groups.notes: Spanish/European descent; concentrated in cities; elite families (traditionally conservative Granada vs liberal León)

ethnic_groups.name: Black/Afro-Nicaraguan
ethnic_groups.notes: Caribbean coast (Bluefields, Puerto Cabezas); English-speaking; Creole culture; Garífuna presence; historically autonomous from Pacific side

ethnic_groups.name: Indigenous
ethnic_groups.notes: Miskito (largest, autonomous regions RACCN/RACCS), Mayangna/Sumu, Rama (nearly extinct), Chorotega, Subtiaba; Caribbean coast autonomy 1987; Sandinista conflict with Miskito (1980s forced relocations)

country_profile.notes_unique: Largest Central American country; William Walker burned Granada 1856 ('Here was Granada'); Augusto César Sandino (guerrilla who fought US Marines 1927-33, assassinated by Somoza, inspired FSLN); Somoza dynasty 1936-79 (43 years, 3 generations: Anastasio Sr., Luis, Anastasio Jr. 'Tachito'); Sandinista Revolution 1979 (FSLN overthrew Somoza); Contra War 1980s (Reagan's 'freedom fighters', 30,000+ dead, Iran-Contra scandal, Ollie North, US mined harbors); Daniel Ortega authoritarian since 2007 (dynastic with wife Rosario Murillo as VP); 2018 protests (355+ killed); largest Catholic-Protestant schism in Central America

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global. 'rank' = 1 is best/largest.

current_leader.name: Daniel Ortega
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: FSLN; Sandinista comandante (1979 revolution); turned authoritarian; wife Rosario Murillo co-president as VP; eliminated term limits; jailed opposition (2021 election farce); Catholic Church repression; exiled dissidents; compared to Somoza; international pariah; oldest caudillo in Americas

former_leaders.name: Enrique Bolaños
former_leaders.notes: PLC; prosecuted predecessor Alemán (corruption); broke with patron; weak presidency

former_leaders.name: Arnoldo Alemán
former_leaders.notes: PLC; convicted of corruption; pact with Ortega (divided power); house arrest; still politically active

former_leaders.name: Violeta Barrios de Chamorro
former_leaders.notes: UNO coalition; first woman president in Americas; widow of La Prensa editor Pedro Joaquín Chamorro (assassinated by Somoza); defeated Ortega 1990 (stunned world); reconciliation; economic stabilization; family divided politically

former_leaders.name: Daniel Ortega
former_leaders.notes: FSLN; junta coordinator then president; Contra War; economy collapsed; lost 1990 election; conceded (surprising); returned 2007 as different person (authoritarian)

former_leaders.name: Junta of National Reconstruction
former_leaders.notes: FSLN-led; collective leadership post-Somoza; Ortega, Violeta Chamorro, others

former_leaders.name: Anastasio Somoza Debayle ('Tacho II' or 'Tachito')
former_leaders.notes: Last Somoza; West Point graduate; embezzled earthquake relief 1972; brutal National Guard; fled July 1979 (assassinated in Paraguay 1980); dynasty ended

former_leaders.name: Luis Somoza Debayle
former_leaders.notes: Middle Somoza; succeeded father; cardiac arrest; less brutal than father/brother

former_leaders.name: Anastasio Somoza García ('Tacho I')
former_leaders.notes: Dynasty founder; National Guard commander; assassinated Sandino 1934; US-backed; accumulated vast wealth; assassinated 1956 by poet Rigoberto López Pérez
